events.content:
Done. Next.js 16's built-in View Transitions require React canary `<ViewTransition>`, so I used the native `document.startViewTransition` API instead:

- `app/transition-link.tsx`: intercepts clicks, records direction on `<html data-nav-direction>`, wraps `router.push` in `startViewTransition` (bails to normal nav when unsupported or reduced-motion)
- Shared element: `view-transition-name: product-image-<slug>` on thumbnails (`app/ProductGrid.tsx:15`) and hero (`app/product/[slug]/page.tsx:49`) → browser morphs between them; morph styled in `app/globals.css`
- Directional slides: forward = old slides out left, back = old slides out right, keyed off the data attribute
- Suspense: `.reveal-content` + `@starting-style` fades/slides skeleton→content reveals
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` kills all view-transition pseudo-animations, reveals, and skeleton pulses; JS skips the transition entirely

Typecheck and build pass; verified names render in served HTML.

- Directional slides: forward = old slides out left, back = old slides out right, keyed off the data attribute
- Suspense: `.reveal-content` + `@starting-style` fades/slides skeleton→content reveals
- `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` kills all view-transition pseudo-animations, reveals, and skeleton pulses; JS skips the transition entirely
